author: The Linux Foundation
description:
Sponsored by Harness

AI coding tools are helping engineering teams create and ship software at unprecedented speed. But our research from 700 enterprise practitioners and engineering leaders reveals a troubling counterweight: 71% say releases or production issues require developers to work evenings or weekends at least weekly, while more than half report frequent or constant burnout.

The surprising finding is that developers do not blame AI. The teams experiencing the most burnout are also among its most enthusiastic users. The real problem is the widening mismatch between AI-scale code generation and delivery systems still dependent on manual testing, fragmented tools, human-operated releases, and reactive incident response.

In this session, attendees will learn:
Why after-hours work should be treated as a software-delivery metric
How high deployment velocity can conceal weak stability and growing rework
Why AI adoption amplifies the strengths and weaknesses of the underlying deli
title: LF Live Webinar: Fast, Fragile, and Burned Out: The Human Cost of AI-Scale Delivery
